 Judgment

The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Lakshmikanth.J.D S/o late Dasegowda, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:

sentences.text: On 27.04.2023 at about 07.20 p.m, when said Lakshmikanth.J.D was proceeding on his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-06-EF-5589 to go to Yadiyur to Hemavathi Cross on the left side of the road and when (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 he reached NH-75, Hassan - Bengaluru Road, in front of Mayura Hotel, Yadiyur Hobli, Kunigal Taluk, Tumkur District, at that time one Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-09-EZ-2586 was going on the same road, driven by its rider at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Motor Cycle of said Lakshmikanth.J.D.

Due to impact, he fell down on the road, at the same time the driver of one Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 came at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came on the same road and ran over said Lakshmikanth.J.D.
Immediately after the accident the Lakshmikanth.J.D was shifted to BGS hospital, Bellur Cross, Mandya District, but he was died in the hospital.

The petitioners have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/-
towards hospital, ambulance, medical, conveyance, food, nourishment, funeral and other incidental charges.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 58 years and was doing Agriculturist, businessman and Archaka of Jalageramma Temple, Yadiyur and earning sum of Rs.1,00,000/- p.m and he is the only earning member of the family.
Due to untimely death of deceased, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.

The petitioner No.1 being wife,
petitioners No.2 and 3 being major sons, petitioner No.4 is (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 married daughter and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of offending Motor Cycle and driving of offending Car by its driver and in this regard the Amruthur Police have registered a case against rider/driver of both vehicles.
The respondents No.1 and 3 being the owners and respondents No.2 and 4 being the insurers of both the offending vehicles
, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- with costs and interest.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 3 did not appeared and hence were placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondents No.2 and 4 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels and filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and admits that this respondent is the insurer of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-09-EZ-2586 and the liability if any is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that as per Charge sheet and Sketch the entire negligence is on the part of deceased/rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-06-EF-5589 was riding in rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle, fell on the road, at that time driver of Car (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 who was coming from back side ran over on him and no actionable negligence can be attributed against rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-09-EZ-2586.

The deceased and driver of car were solely responsible for the accident and hence the petition is liable to be dismissed against this respondent on this score alone and further denied age, occupation, income of deceased and treatment taken by the deceased,
expenses incurred by the petitioners and dependency of the petitioners and manner of accident and involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.
Hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.

sentences.text:
The respondent No.4 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and denies that the Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 stood insured with them as on the date of accident and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the driver of the offending Car was not holding valid and effective driving licence and hence the owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and further denied the alleged accident,
negligence of the drover of offending Car, age, avocation and income of the deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and treatment (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 taken by the deceased, dependency of the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners and contended that the Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 was not at all involved in the accident and the jurisdictional Police have filed false Charge sheet against the car colluding with petitioner and owner of the vehicle and on the date of accident the deceased was proceedings on his Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-06-EF-5589, at that time one Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-09-EZ-2586 was proceeding at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased Motor Cycle from back side, due to which he fell down, at the same time one Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, came from same direction and ran over on the deceased.
The compensation claimed is exorbitant and hence prays to dismiss the petition against respondent No.4 with costs.

06. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether petitioners proves that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Lakshmikanth.J.D S/o late Dasegowda?
 (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2976/2024  02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Lakshmikanth.J.D S/o late Dasegowda was died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 27.04.2023 at about 07.20 p.m, on NH-75, Hassan - Bengaluru Road, in front of Mayura Hotel, Yadiyur, Kunigal Taluk,
Tumkur District, due to rash and negligent riding of Motor Cycle bearing No.
KA-09-EZ- 2586 by its rider and driving of Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?
07. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 18 documents as Ex.P.1 to 18 and closed their side evidence.

sentences.text: By way of rebuttal, the respondents No.2 and 4 got examined their Officials as RW.1 and 2 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed their side evidence.

09. Heard both sides.
10.

My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.2976/2024  Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order  for the following:-
 REASONS  11. Issue No.1 :- Petitioner No.1 in her affidavit stated that, petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are the major sons and married daughter and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased.

To prove the said facts, she has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of herself, deceased and other petitioners, Ration card,
DL of deceased as per Ex.P.11 to 18.

In her cross-examination she has stated that petitioners No.2 to 4 are married and her mother-in-law is residing with her brother-in-law and denied to the suggestion that petitioners No.2 to 5 are not depending on the income of her husband.
But as per the recent Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court even the major sons and married daughters are entitled to claim compensation for the death of their parents on all heads.
These documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioners are the legal heirs and (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 dependents on the deceased.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

12. Issue No.2:- PW.1 filed affidavit by stating that due to the negligence of rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-09-EZ-2586 and driver of the Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 accident took place and deceased died in the accident.

In her cross- examination nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of the petitioners regarding rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Motor Cycle and driving by the driver of the car and deceased sustained injuries, later died.

On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 FIR registered at Amruthur Police against rider of offending Motor Cycle and driver of Car for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.134(a & b)
and 187 of IMV Act.

Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of Motor Cycle and driving of the driver of the offending car the accident took place, in which the deceased sustained injuries and later died.
Ex.P.3 to 6 are the Spot Mahazar, Sketch and Seizer Mahazars shows the place of accident on NH-75, Mangalore - Bengaluru Road, in front of Mayura Hotel, Chankenahalli, Yadiyur Hobli, Kunigal Taluk
and after investigation the Police have seized both the offending (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 vehicles after investigation, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.7 is IMV report shows involvement of three vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P.8 is Lalithamma vs Preetham Kishor H N on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58915241/

sentences.text: 5 Inquest report of the deceased Lakshmikanth.J.D.
Ex.P.9 is Post mortem report of deceased Lakshmikanth.J.D shows the cause of death is kept pending for want of RFSL report.

Ex.P.10 is the Charge sheet filed against the rider of the Motor Cycle and driver of the Car for the offences punishable U/s 279, 304A of IPC and Sec.134(a & b) and 187 of IMV Act for the reasons that the driver of the car after caused the accident has not informed the accident to the Police and did not taken the injured to the hospital for providing treatment, without stopping the vehicle fled away from the accident spot.

These documents clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the rider of the Motor Cycle and driver of the Car and deceased sustained injuries and later died.
Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Lakshmikanth.J.D, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 about 58 years and was doing Agriculturist, businessman and Archaka of Jalageramma Temple, Yadiyur and earning sum of Rs.1,00,000/- p.m and has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards hospital, ambulance, medical, conveyance, food, nourishment,
funeral and other incidental charges.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss and mental agony.
14. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.14 Aadhaar card and Ex.P.16 Driving licence of deceased.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence,
said documents can be relied upon and according to which his date of birth is mentioned as 10.09.1964.
The alleged accident occurred on 27.04.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased is 53 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased is 59 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 years is "9".
15.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the deceased, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2023 to be taken as Rs.16,000/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.16,000/-..
16.

In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 are the sons and daughter and petitioner No.5 is the mother of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

sentences.text: Since deceased was (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 aged about 59 years and was working as self employee at the time of accident, 10% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,000 + 1,600) = Rs.17,600/-.

Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are five dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.17,600 - Rs.4,400) =
Rs.13,200/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.13,200/-.
As the deceased was aged about 59 years, the multiplier of 9 would have to be applied.

Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of (Rs.13,200 x 12 x 9)
Rs.14,25,600/- is awarded towards loss of dependency.

17. In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & Others case, in respect to loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses, the aforesaid amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every 3 years.

sentences.text: Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 loss of consortium and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
18. The claimant No.1 is the wife, claimants No.2 to 4 are the sons and daughter and claimant No.5 is the mother of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 and 5 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of spousal consortium and filial consortium.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioners No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/-
each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

Ltd., V/s. Pranay Sethi & others case has calculated compensation as under;

sentences.text: Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.16,81,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
Insurance Companies have contended that the rider of the offending Motor cycle and driver of the offending Car had no driving licence to drive the vehicles at the time of accident.
On perusal of Charge sheet at Ex.P.10 the Investigation Officer has not quoted any (SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 sections against both rider and driver for not having driving licence.
As per Ex.R.2 and 4 policies of both Motor Cycle and Car is valid as on the date of accident.

In this regard,
the respondent No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.1 and in his chief- examination evidence he has admitted issuance policy to the offending Motor Cycle and the same is valid as on the date of accident and in his cross-examination he clearly stated that the Police have wrongly filed Charge sheet against their insured vehicle and as per IMV report their insured got damaged at front side and they have issued notice to the rider/owner.

21. Further, the Legal Manager of the respondent No.4 Insurance Company is examined as RW.2 and in his chief-examination he has stated that as per Motor Vehicle Inspection report no any damages were found at the time of inspection, which shows the non-involvement of Car in the allged accident and in his cross-examination he admits that as per records when the deceased fell down from the Motor Cycle, their insured vehicle ran over on him.
But the Investigation Officer has filed Charge sheet against their insured vehicle for rash and negligent driving and (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 caused accident.
Hence, the contention of RW.1 and RW.2 is untenable.

22. Therefore, the respondents No.1 and 3 being the owners and respondents No.2 and 4 being the insurers of the offending Motor Cycle and offending Car are jointly and severally liable to pay total compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, since policy of offending vehicles was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondents No.2 and 4 being the insurers of offending vehicles shall deposit above said compensation amount of Rs.16,81,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.3 partly in affirmative.

23. Issue No.4: In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,81,400/- (Rupees Sixteen lakhs eighty one (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 thousand and four hundred only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents No.2 and 4 shall deposit above said compensation amount equally with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

sentences.text: The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 being the sons and daughter and petitioner No.5 being the mother of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 60-10- 10-10-10, in the award amount together with interest.

On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount of petitioners No.2 to 5 is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.Lakshmikanth.J.D S/o late Dasegowda, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
Due to impact, he fell down on the road, at the same time the driver of one Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 came at high speed, in rash and negligent manner, came on the same road and ran over said Lakshmikanth.J.D.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of offending Motor Cycle and driving of offending Car by its driver and in this regard the Amruthur Police have registered a case against rider/driver of both vehicles.
The respondent No.4 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioner and denies that the Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 stood insured with them as on the date of accident and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the driver of the offending Car was not holding valid and effective driving licence and hence the owner has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and further denied the alleged accident,
negligence of the drover of offending Car, age, avocation and income of the deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and treatment (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 taken by the deceased, dependency of the petitioners and expenses incurred by the petitioners and contended that the Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 was not at all involved in the accident and the jurisdictional Police have filed false Charge sheet against the car colluding with petitioner and owner of the vehicle and on the date of accident the deceased was proceedings on his Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-06-EF-5589, at that time one Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-09-EZ-2586 was proceeding at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and hit the deceased Motor Cycle from back side, due to which he fell down, at the same time one Car bearing No.KA-02-MN-2514 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, came from same direction and ran over on the deceased.

14. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The alleged accident occurred on 27.04.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased is 53 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased is 59 years as on the date of accident.
As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 56 to 60 years is "9".
15.
In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

Since deceased was (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 aged about 59 years and was working as self employee at the time of accident, 10% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (16,000 + 1,600) = Rs.17,600/-.
Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are five dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.17,600 - Rs.4,400) =
Rs.13,200/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.13,200/-.
Accordingly, in the head of loss of estate, (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 loss of consortium and funeral expenses, 10% is enhanced for period of every 3 years.
Therefore, petitioners No.1 and 5 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each towards loss of spousal consortium and filial consortium.
However, since policy of offending vehicles was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondents No.2 and 4 being the insurers of offending vehicles shall deposit above said compensation amount of Rs.16,81,400/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.

23. Issue No.4: In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 to 3, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.16,81,400/- (Rupees Sixteen lakhs eighty one (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.2976/2024 thousand and four hundred only)
with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents No.2 and 4 shall deposit above said compensation amount equally with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
The petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioners No.2 to 4 being the sons and daughter and petitioner No.5 being the mother of the deceased were apportioned the compensation in the ratio of 60-10- 10-10-10, in the award amount together with interest.
On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to her account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in her name.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount of petitioners No.2 to 5 is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released in their favour through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
